binary.architecture: stub EXE that loads libllama-server-impl.dll + libllama.dll + ggml-cuda.dll (from cuda_v12 subdirectory)

flags_confirmed.--context-shift: present but applies only to infinite text generation (n_predict=-1), NOT single-request prompts

gpu_inference.requirement: PATH must include cuda_v12 directory; GGML_BACKEND_DL_PATH must point to cuda_v12; server must run with cuda_v12 as working directory or in PATH
gpu_inference.note: Without cuda_v12 in environment, server silently falls back to CPU with no error — GPU warning appears in log only

kv_precision_measurement.method: VRAM delta between ctx=4096 and ctx=32768, n_slots=1, n_gpu_layers=99, single server per measurement

f16.deviation_note: 2% below architectural. Qwen3 SWA enabled by default (--swa-full not set); SWA layers maintain smaller window, reducing total KV. Build-specific: b1-f8def7fe1.

q8_0.deviation_note: 10% above architectural. Per-block quantization metadata (scale factors) stored at full precision. Metadata overhead becomes a larger fraction of total KV at lower element precision.

q4_0.deviation_note: 21% above architectural. Per-block overhead is largest at q4 — each block header scales by block count, not element count. Overhead-to-element ratio is worst at highest compression.

kv_precision_measurement.key_finding: Quantization flags take effect. Measured f16->q4_0 reduction is 3.24x, not the architectural 4x. Provisioning based on architectural bytes-per-token overestimates what quantization buys. The shortfall grows with quantization depth. The provisioning table must carry both architectural and measured columns; the gap between them is the finding.
kv_precision_measurement.implication_for_literature: Published token-precision literature cites architectural ratios (2x for q8, 4x for q4). This study cannot confirm these ratios at their stated values. Use measured ratios for any hardware provisioning calculation on this model and build.

inference_comparison_vs_ollama.method: /v1/chat/completions endpoint (OpenAI-compatible) on both runtimes, same model weights, identical system prompt, temperature=0, seed=42
inference_comparison_vs_ollama.conclusion: llama-server and ollama are equivalent runtimes on this host for single-turn inference at full context. Outputs are identical, prompt token counts match, the same chat template is applied. Earlier prompt-truncation results are valid under llama-server.

context_shift_behavior.test: Submitted prompt of 38031 tokens to server with ctx-size=8192, with and without --context-shift flag
context_shift_behavior.result_without_flag: HTTP 400: request (38031 tokens) exceeds the available context size (8192 tokens)
context_shift_behavior.conclusion: Context shift in this build applies ONLY to infinite text generation (n_predict=-1), not to single-request prompts that exceed the context window. A pre-built prompt larger than ctx-size is rejected regardless of the --context-shift flag. This is the same behavior as the ollama wrapper. Context shift is not a mechanism for handling large RAG artifacts in single-turn inference.
context_shift_behavior.implication_for_stage_2: Stage 2 eviction experiments cannot use the single-request format to trigger context shift. Two viable approaches: (a) incremental multi-turn conversations that accumulate context across requests, using llama-server's KV cache reuse; (b) reframe as streaming eviction with n_predict=-1 and a sufficiently long generation. The programme's framing that llama-server 'performs context shift when a session exceeds its allocated window' applies to the streaming/accumulation case, not the batch inference case. All prior single-turn experiments submitted truncated prompts, which is methodologically consistent with the single-request constraint that applies to both runtimes.

launch_recipe.path_setup: PATH must include lib/ollama/cuda_v12 and lib/ollama; GGML_BACKEND_DL_PATH=lib/ollama/cuda_v12
launch_recipe.working_directory: lib/ollama/cuda_v12 (or any directory where cuda_v12 DLLs are resolvable)
